newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B index falls at noon, awaits results.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index falls at noon, awaits results.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index ended Friday morning a shade lower in light trade, driven by investor caution ahead of the weekend when some listed firms could release interim results, analysts said.
The index edged down 0.67 points or 0.50 percent to 132.97 points on thin turnover of HK$18.0 million.
The Chinese yuan-based A share index gained 0.78 points or 0.19 percent to 415.91 points on turnover of 3.6 billion yuan.
"People seem to be more cautious ahead of the weekend when some firms may release interim results," a trader at China Guotai Securities said.
"The (B share) index is likely going to move sideways in the near future while sentiment remains cautious," the trader said.
The first-half reports, which must be published by August 30, have spurred speculation but many people have stayed on the sidelines to get a fuller picture, analysts said.
"The (B) index may ease a bit in the afternoon judging by the light trading volume," an analyst at China Securities said.
"Many funds have dried up after the recent drive against stock-related speculation," she said.
Beijing unleashed a series of measures starting in May to crack down on market irregularities, and banned many institutions from trading in the stock markets.
In the B share market, property concern Hainan Pearl River Enterprises Co Ltd was the biggest loser, sliding HK$0.10 or 5.13 percent to HK$1.85.
In the A share market, distillery Hunan Jiuguijiu, which listed on Friday, jumped to 30.30 yuan compared with the 8.0 yuan offer price.
